title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect, reconnect/resume and server timeouts
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: Improve streaming stability and behavior at the API surface when clients cancel, disconnect unexpectedly, or reconnect/resume. This PR centralizes lifecycle controls in the streaming runtime and OpenAI compatibility layer, adds explicit server-side timeouts and resume windows, and hardens tool/function-calling streams against half-closed connections. Summary of changes: 1) connection manager: track per-stream session IDs, last-active timestamps, and graceful resume windows; 2) client cancel semantics: introduce deterministic CancelAck message and ensure KV cache / running compute is aborted within configured cancellation grace; 3) disconnect handling: retain short-lived session state for resume (configurable via STREAM_RESUME_WINDOW_MS) and drain in-flight batches to minimize token duplication; 4) reconnect/resume: negotiate resume token and offset, fall back to Idempotent re-run when resume not possible; 5) server timeouts: introduce per-request socket idle timeout and per-stream total timeout with updated defaults to match OpenAI semantics; 6) SDKs: python/ts clients updated to send resume token and to retry idempotently on reconnect; 7) docs: add OpenAI-compat streaming lifecycle doc and migration notes. Checklist: - [x] design review and linear tasks linked - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] e2e reconnection test in perf-canary - [x] docs and SDK updates - [x] observability metrics and tracing events Related: Linear ENG-4281 (streaming lifecycle controls), ENG-4302 (openai compat resume semantics). See docs: docs/openai-compat/streaming-lifecycle.md and issues noted in the perf-canary run. No user-facing API changes beyond additional optional resume semantics and a new header for resume tokens.

merge_commit_message: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel/disconnect/reconnect/resume + server timeouts\n\nAdds connection manager, cancel ack, resume negotiation, server timeouts, SDKs and docs. Resolves ENG-4281 ENG-4302.
release_notes: Stability improvements for streaming connections: deterministic client cancel ack, configurable resume window, reconnect/resume support with idempotent fallback, and server-side timeouts. SDKs updated to support resume tokens. No breaking API changes.
notes_for_operators: Operators: STREAM_RESUME_WINDOW_MS default is 30000 (30s). Increase only if downstream networks are unreliable. New metrics: stream.resume.attempt, stream.resume.success, stream.cancel.ack, stream.timeout.expired. Observe token-dup metrics when enabling long resume windows.
security_considerations: Resume tokens are short-lived opaque strings bound to session IDs and verified server-side. No PII is retained in resume metadata. Added extra checks to prevent session token reuse.
backout_plan: Revert head branch and a hotfix that disables resume window by setting STREAM_RESUME_WINDOW_MS=0 for hosted main if regressions observed. Metrics are in place to detect increase in token duplication or failed resumes.
notes: Deployed behind feature flag 'streaming_lifecycle_controls' for staged rollout. Monitored for 72 hours on canary and 7 days in staged rollout before full release.
